data.name: Gunjika
data.gender_notes: Gunjika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gunjika is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Gunj' which means 'sound' or 'vibration'. The suffix 'ka' denotes 'one who produces' or 'bringer of'. This name signifies the one who brings the sound or victory in any given situation. The name Gunjika carries the meaning “Sound of Victory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gunjika usually hope their child will grow to embody sound of victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gunjika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sound of Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gunjika total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Gunjika was a legendary heroine in the Indian epic Mahabharata who was known for her exceptional archery skills. She was the wife of Bahlika, a king in the kingdom of Matsya. When Bhishma, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, lay down on the bed of arrows, Gunjika shot an arrow through his eye from a great distance, thus fulfilling a promise made to Bhishma by her father.
